findings.title: approve shows a revoke to the zero address as 'Allow 0x000… to withdraw and transfer'.
findings.evidence: NonfungiblePositionManager._approve: `_positions[tokenId].operator = to;`. approve(0, id) clears the operator. The descriptor says "Allow {to} to withdraw and transfer position NFT {tokenId}" and has no special case for address(0).
findings.fix: Add a message or a label for the zero address on `to`, for example "None (revokes operator)", or say in the intent that the zero address removes the operator.

cases.notes: The operator approval for NFT #1390670 is shown with the right operator and position.

formats.key: collect((uint256 tokenId,address recipient,uint128 amount0Max,uint128 amount1Max) params)
effects: Sends the fees and tokens owed to position `tokenId`, up to amount0Max of token0 and amount1Max of token1, from the pool to `recipient`.
A zero recipient keeps the tokens in the position manager, where any caller can sweep them.
Lowers the amounts owed to the position by the collected amounts.
Any ETH sent stays in the contract. The screen shows it only when the value is not zero.
formats.shown: Collect up to raw amounts of token0 and token1 owed to the position, sent to the recipient, plus a note about the zero address.

findings.title: collect never names the two tokens received, because they come from position storage.
findings.evidence: Case 2: the signer received 564070 WBTC (0.0056 WBTC) and 470556602 USDC (470.56 USDC). The screen says only "token0" and "token1 (raw units)". In collect, `poolKey = _poolIdToPoolKey[position.poolId]` comes from storage.
findings.fix: No fix is possible in the descriptor. ERC-7730 cannot read the position's tokens from storage.

findings.title: collect puts the uint128 maximum, a 39-digit number, into the intent sentence twice.
findings.evidence: Case 2 interpolatedIntent: "Collect up to 340282366920938463463374607431768211455 token0 and up to 340282366920938463463374607431768211455 token1 (raw units)...". The code caps at tokensOwed: `params.amount0Max > tokensOwed0 ? tokensOwed0 : params.amount0Max`.
findings.fix: Take the raw maximums out of interpolatedIntent, for example "Collect tokens owed to position {params.tokenId}, sent to {params.recipient}". Keep them as fields only.

findings.title: collect always shows the zero-address warning, even when the recipient is a normal address.
findings.evidence: Descriptor interpolatedIntent ends with "The zero address keeps them in this contract, where any caller can sweep them". Code: `params.recipient == address(0) ? address(this) : params.recipient`.
findings.fix: Show the zero-address meaning on the Recipient field, with a label or a message, and take it out of the always-shown sentence.

cases.notes: The direction, the bound and the recipient are right. The assets WBTC and USDC are never named.

formats.key: increaseLiquidity((uint256 tokenId,uint256 amount0Desired,uint256 amount1Desired,uint256 amount0Min,uint256 amount1Min,uint256 deadline) params)
effects: Takes up to amount0Desired of token0 and up to amount1Desired of token1 from the signer (at least the minimums) and sends them to the pool.
Adds the new liquidity to position `tokenId`, which can belong to any owner. No owner check exists.
For a WETH pair, ETH sent can pay the WETH part. Leftover ETH stays in the contract unless refundETH follows.

findings.title: increaseLiquidity never names the tokens taken, because the pool tokens are in position storage.
findings.evidence: Case 5: the signer sent 0.2263 stkAAVE and 0.4654 AAVE. The screen shows "Add up to 226270246449117879 token0 and up to 465376757948285913 token1 (raw units)". In increaseLiquidity, `poolKey = _poolIdToPoolKey[position.poolId]` comes from storage.

findings.title: increaseLiquidity adds funds to any position, and the screen does not show who owns it.

formats.key: mint((address token0,address token1,uint24 fee,int24 tickLower,int24 tickUpper,uint256 amount0Desired,uint256 amount1Desired,uint256 amount0Min,uint256 amount1Min,address recipient,uint256 deadline) params)
effects: Takes up to amount0Desired of token0 and amount1Desired of token1 from the signer (at least the minimums) and sends them to the pool.
Mints a new position NFT to `recipient`.
When token0 or token1 is WETH, the contract's ETH balance (msg.value) pays that part instead of the signer's WETH. Leftover ETH stays in the contract, where any caller can take it with refundETH.
formats.shown: Add up to X token0 and Y token1 to a new position for the recipient. Fields show the maximums, minimums, fee, ticks, deadline, and ETH Sent when the value is not zero.

findings.title: mint does not say that ETH sent pays the WETH side or that leftover ETH stays claimable.
findings.evidence: PeripheryPayments.pay: `if (token == WETH9 && address(this).balance >= value) { IWETH9(WETH9).deposit{value: value}(); ...}`. refundETH sends the whole balance to any msg.sender. The descriptor shows "Maximum to Add … WETH" and a separate "ETH Sent".
findings.fix: Change the ETH Sent label to "ETH Sent (pays WETH side; refund in same batch)", and add a test with a WETH pair and a non-zero value.

findings.title: mint shows the price range only as raw ticks.
findings.evidence: Case 6 shows "Lower Tick -288400" and "Upper Tick -286600". No ERC-7730 format turns a tick into a price.
findings.fix: No fix is possible in the descriptor.

effects: Delegatecalls each inner call on the position manager, in order, with the signer as msg.sender and the same msg.value for every call.
Sends the ETH value once. Each inner call has the effects of its own function.
Reverts everything if one inner call fails.
formats.shown: Send {@.value} and run every action below, with ETH Sent and each inner call decoded as an Action.

findings.title: multicall is tested only with an empty batch, so no nested rendering is checked.
findings.evidence: Case 19: "multicall, empty batch (encoded)", data length 0. The usual batches, such as decreaseLiquidity+collect+sweepToken or mint+refundETH with ETH, have no test.
findings.fix: Add multicall test cases with real batches, including one with a non-zero value.

findings.title: multicall passes the full outer ETH value to every inner action, so ETH Sent can repeat.
findings.evidence: The descriptor has `"amountPath": "@.value"` on `data.[]`. Each inner payable format shows "ETH Sent" when the value is not zero. Multicall.multicall: `address(this).delegatecall(data[i])` keeps msg.value.
findings.fix: No change is needed. The repeated value matches the delegatecall behaviour, but it may make the signer think ETH is sent more than once.
